extracted.intended_audience: graduate and advanced-undergraduate students in measure theory / real analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Constructing and proving the Riesz Representation Theorem: given a positive linear functional on Ccom(X) for a locally compact Hausdorff space X, build a unique regular Borel measure µ with `(f)=∫ f dµ, establish its regularity and additivity, and extend it from compact sets to the Borel σ-algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riesz Representation Theorem (statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ` is a positive linear functional on Ccom(X), then there exists a unique regular Borel measure µ on X such that `(f) = ∫_X f dµ for all f in Ccom(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness and regularity are part of the conclusion. The proof constructs µ from ` by first defining µ on compact sets, proving algebraic and regularity identities, extending to the ring generated by compact sets, and then to the Borel σ-algebra; parallels the construction of Lebesgue measure on R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain and test-function space requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The underlying space X must be a locally compact Hausdorff space; Ccom(X) denotes the vector space of continuous scalar-valued functions on X having compact support (support = closure of {x: f(x) ≠ 0}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positivity for a linear functional ` means `(f) ≥ 0 whenever f ≥ 0. The scalars may be real or complex; the construction focuses on positive linear functionals on Ccom(X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Borel σ-algebra and ring of elementary sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the σ-algebra B(X) to be the smallest σ-algebra containing all compact subsets of X. Let K(X) be the smallest ring (algebra) containing compact sets; its members (elementary sets) are finite disjoint unions of sets of the form K \ L with K and L compact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K(X) plays the role of the 'ring generated by bounded intervals' in R. In proofs one works initially on K(X) and then extends to B(X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of µ on compact sets
rubrics_metrics.description: For a compact set K, define µ(K) = inf{ `(f) : f ∈ Ccom(X), f ≥ I_K } (one may restrict to functions taking values in [0,1]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 11.8 shows the infimum can be computed over functions that equal 1 on some neighborhood of K; this is crucial for later limit and additivity arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity of Borel measures (definition used)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Borel measure µ is regular if for every Borel set E, µ(E) = sup{ µ(K) : K ⊆ E, K compact } and for every σ-bounded Borel set E, µ(E) = inf{ µ(U) : U ⊇ E, U open and σ-bounded }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularity is the property ultimately proved for the measure associated to `. The σ-bounded condition (countable union of compacts) enters in the outer approximation by open sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite additivity identity for compact sets
rubrics_metrics.description: For compact sets K1 and K2, µ(K1 ∪ K2) = µ(K1) + µ(K2) − µ(K1 ∩ K2) (equivalently µ(K1 ∪ K2) + µ(K1 ∩ K2) = µ(K1) + µ(K2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identity (Lemma 11.9) is proved by approximating indicator functions by continuous functions and using linearity of `. Iteration yields analogous inclusion–exclusion formulas for any finite family of compact sets (Lemma 11.10). This is the core algebraic property needed to define µ on the ring K(X) consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation identity for open sets with compact closure
rubrics_metrics.description: If U is open and has compact closure, then µ(U) equals the supremum of µ(K) over compact K ⊆ U; equivalently µ(U) = sup{ `(f) : f ∈ Ccom(X), 0 ≤ f ≤ I_U } when U has compact closure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives inner regularity for such U (and is used to show eventual regularity on the whole class). The proof reduces open U to approximating compact subsets and continuous functions supported in U (Lemma 11.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to functions equal to 1 near compact sets
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing µ(K) as inf{ `(f) : f ≥ I_K }, it suffices to take the infimum over functions f ∈ Ccom(X) with values in [0,1] that equal 1 on some neighborhood of K (Lemma 11.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This localized restriction is essential to pass to uniform limits and to use Dini-type arguments; it avoids needing arbitrary global approximants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of positive linear functional on uniformly convergent sequences with fixed compact support
rubrics_metrics.description: If (f_n) is a sequence in Ccom(X) with support(f_n) ⊆ K for a fixed compact K and f_n → f uniformly, then `(f_n) → `(f) (Lemma 11.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses existence of F ∈ Ccom(X) identically 1 on K and positivity/linearity of `. This continuity property permits passage of limits when approximating indicators by continuous functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dini-type uniform convergence for monotone sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If (f_n) is a sequence in Ccom(X) supported in a fixed compact K and f_n decreases pointwise to 0, then f_n → 0 uniformly (Lemma 11.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compactness-based uniform convergence (Dini's theorem variant) is used to justify limit manipulations of `(f_n) and to derive additivity identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topological approximations: compact Gδ and open Fσ constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any compact Gδ K can be written as intersection of a decreasing sequence of bounded open sets Un with Un ⊇ closure(Un) ⊇ K; any bounded open Fσ U can be written as union of an increasing sequence of compact sets K_n with K_n ⊆ interior(K_{n+1}) ⊆ U (Lemmas 11.6–11.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These decompositions are used to build the Ccom approximants (functions equal to 1 nearby K or supported inside U) needed in the µ(K) and µ(U) constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of the ring K(X)
rubrics_metrics.description: K(X) (the ring generated by compact sets) consists exactly of finite disjoint unions of sets of the form K \ L with K and L compact; equivalently it is the smallest ring containing all bounded open sets (Lemma 11.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This algebraic description justifies representing general elementary sets in a canonical finite disjoint union form to define µ additively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and well-definedness of µ on K(X) (general elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an element of K(X) is written as a finite disjoint union of K_j \ L_j (K_j, L_j compact), define µ(∪_j (K_j \ L_j)) := ∑_j (µ(K_j) − µ(L_j)). This definition is well-defined and yields a nonnegative additive set function on K(X) (Lemma 11.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtlety arises because the K_j need not be pairwise disjoint a priori; the lemmas and inclusion–exclusion identities ensure the formula is independent of the chosen decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete additivity on the generating ring implies extendability
rubrics_metrics.description: Once µ is shown to be completely additive on the ring K(X) and finite-valued there, apply the Extension Theorem to extend µ to the σ-ring (and then canonically to the σ-algebra B(X)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This step parallels the Lebesgue measure construction: establishing complete additivity (countable additivity) on the ring is the technical core; thereafter standard extension results give a Borel measure with the regularity properties proven earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: σ-bounded and bounded set notions (for outer regularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set E ⊆ X is bounded if it is contained in some compact set; E is σ-bounded if it is contained in a countable union of compact sets. Regularity's outer approximation uses σ-bounded open supersets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The µ constructed is finite on compact sets and outer regular approximations consider only σ-bounded open sets to ensure finiteness when taking infima.
